title: Daily clocks missed more 30-kt wind-loss than wind-gain labels in eastern Pacific HURDAT2 storms in 1982-2023
abstract: We tested an Atlantic sampling result in a separate eastern Pacific storm sample. A valid 24-hour window had five six-hour tropical storm or hurricane records. Net wind changes of at least 30 kt defined gain and loss labels. Among 627 eligible EP storms in 1982-2023, 268 had gain labels and 268 had loss labels. Four daily UTC clocks missed a mean 23.7% of gain labels and 31.6% of loss labels. The paired difference was 7.93 percentage points, with a conditional 95% year-bootstrap interval of 4.20 to 11.67 points. Three-year blocks gave 4.14 to 11.46 points. The result supports the direction of the prior Atlantic result with different storms. At 25 kt, the gap was smaller and its interval included zero. The gap difference between basins was uncertain. This controlled removal of start times does not measure missed true events or identify an ocean or atmosphere process. Wind error, land exposure and storm selection limit the result.

display.caption: Daily-clock sampling loss in two storm samples and eastern Pacific rule checks. Bars and points show aggregate results. Lines show conditional 95% year-bootstrap intervals. AL is the Atlantic reference; EP is the independent storm sample.

citations.reason: We test its Atlantic sampling result in different EP storms and reproduce its Atlantic counts as a code check.
